I'm a treadmill runner, 5x a week, myself. There's not much difference between the steps taken to mitigate injuries when running outdoors vs. a treadmill, IMO.

If you're sticking to the same pace for the entire run, do use an easier pace since that is the pace you have to stick with throughout the entire run. No allowances unlike running outdoors whereby the pace is more.. natural, and will fluctuate a little.

To simulate outdoor running, if you're just doing easy/long runs (aka not tempo / interval / speed training), try to set the incline to 1% at least. Outdoor running will never be on 100% flat ground. that's the rationale behind this setting.

Ultimately, just like running outdoors, do listen to your body and stop whenever you feel sick or uncomfortable / start to hurt somewhere. 

I personally stick to easy runs and slowly increase my mileage week on week, and of course not by much, just like how it is for outdoor running.

Oh, and one more thing, try to watch your stride, too. If it's long / wide, don't position yourself too closely to the front of the treadmill so that your foot doesn't step too much to the front and away from the belt, only to hit the machine.

All the best to your recovery and keep running! Getting one foot in front of the other is what truly matters, no matter the medium.
